linux_runtime_pr209_20261024.scope: Standalone development reconciliation against base478, incorporating linux-baseline and PR209 runtime features; updated2026-10-25. Manifest1-7 with local DIT7 and preserved Llama hi/lo sub-block attention. GGUF Q/K/Q8-head corrections, checked dense head dimensions, flash streams through8192, explicit paired probabilities and unsupported-window refusal. Paired-P300/8192 and real4096-boundary model gates pass; artificial zero-history cosine failure remains. Includes synthetic --bench-kernel seek fix, compact5120 packing regression, and explicit experimental bfp16_hilo block input (9/4 bytes; native F32 output), independent host-pack tests and fail-closed incompatible-scope metadata. Compensated route300/8192/real-boundary gates pass; accepted end-to-end speed remains unmeasured under idle conditions. Bonsai/Hadamard and broad DIT/family acceptance remain open. Not a sequential patch series or default promotion.

gemma4_block_prefill_20261029.note: dense gemm_block cd_preffn / cd_postffn: the block route's FFN-side sandwich norms from the consts (Gemma 4's folded layer_output_scale) instead of the file

gemma4_bringup_dumps_20261029.note: bring-up only: open_qwen36_cli --dump-act all:<prefix> (every layer's whole act) and --dump-kv <prefix> (checkpoint KV rows)

gemma4_compact_gguf_20261029.note: std_perm_gguf packs into the pool's chunk law: 6144-B f32 scales, or 5120-B q4_1-law bf16 scales (RNE, what the f32-scale kernels narrow to on the core) for the compact GGUF view; the branch of linux_runtime_pr209_20261024 without its Llama rotary permute

gemma4_attn_block_20261029.note: dense attn_block prep qkvnorm_rope (Gemma 4): q / k norms from the consts, weightless V norm, score scale, per-layer-type rotation (pair distance) and inv_freq, sliding window (first row, softmax mask, windowed read-back), Q hi / lo; attn_window_test. A diff over base plus the three earlier Gemma 4 patches, unlike the standalone ones

gemma4_prefill_host_20261029.note: the dense block route's host stages, bit-identical: the sandwich joins in one pass a token row (sandwich_rows), the FFN activation's fp64 half under the up projection's dispatch and h = act * up straight into the down projection's tiled x (act_fp64, act_tile), attention_npu's row loops and the K / V tilers over the host threads, and a layer-major prompt for the dense kind (step_gemm_prompt_dense: every block's qkv3, then their attention, then the rest; on for qkvnorm_rope sets, OFLM_OPEN_DENSE_LAYER_MAJOR). A diff over base plus the four earlier Gemma 4 patches

gemma4_bfp16_prefill_20261030.note: the dense block route's GEMMs on gemm_bfp16 (OPEN-PREFILL-BFP16 on the dense kind): manifest_version 4 (the bfp16_gemm pack op, row0 / n_total, and the bfp16 step format with n_pad; a bfp16 step reads exactly a bfp16_gemm weight, dense routes only), bfp16_gemm from a GGUF tensor's own blocks (embed_row) as well as q4nx q4_1 chunks, the activation packer and the c-tiled output read back as [N, T] or token rows, act * up encoded straight into the down projection's A operand (act_bfp16_a), and the prefill route chosen in the GGUF view too, where a GGUF-direct set carries its routes (fast = gemm_block, lean = the variant). bfp16.hpp is the granite branch's (openflowlm-next 07e635b) plus bfp16_c_offset. A diff over base plus the five earlier Gemma 4 patches

gemma4_prefill_pipeline_20261030.note: the dense layer-major prompt step-major (dense_layer_staged, on unless OFLM_OPEN_STAGE_MAJOR=0): qkv3 over every block with each block's attention host half under the next block's GEMM, the attention products over every (block, kv head), then o / up / gate / down over the blocks in pairs, one run outstanding and #1 twins of every x / y / attn_block global (pipeline()); each block's operations unchanged, so the same bits. The bfp16 route's GELU-tanh act in fp32 on AVX2 fused with act * up and the encode (gelu_bfp16_a, OFLM_OPEN_GELU32=0 keeps act_fp64). The A-operand encoders write in memory order and bfp16_encode_block takes its exponent maximum on the vector unit. attn_block's optional kernels_shl: qsplit's hi / lo scores as one product of 2 m rows (OFLM_OPEN_ATTN_SHL=0 off). The bfp16_gemm packer without per-block divisions, and a pack weight zeroes only the bytes no op writes (pools::unwritten). --prefill-mode accurate is lean. Without a bit changed, attention_prep takes rope angles once a position, up writes its own output pair (@up), gate encodes h straight into its down job's x and reuses up's x twin, qkv3 rows go straight into q / k / v (bfp16_rows_parts), and the stacked scores' softmax sums hi + lo as it reads them (softmax_chunk_sum); OFLM_OPEN_PIPE_LOG prints per-step host and wait times. A diff over base plus the six earlier Gemma 4 patches

gemma4_q40_gguf_20261030.note: std_perm_gguf's third chunk law: a 4608-B pool chunk (the Q4_0-native GGUF view, recipes/gemma4.py G4_Q40) holds the bf16 d plane and the codes, the cores taking m = -8 d (gemv_q4.h GEMV_Q4_0_NATIVE, gemm_q4_dequant.h GQD_Q4_0); only Q4_0 tensors pack into it, anything else is refused. gguf_pack_test checks it against the q4_1 law's d plane and codes, that law's m against -8 d, and that a Q4_1 tensor is refused. A diff over base plus the seven earlier Gemma 4 patches

gemma4_kvslice_20261030.note: per-core KV windows (OPEN-ATTN-KVSLICE) in this runtime: the manifest's kernel `kvslice` (2 or 4 rows an element, attnpos only, rb 1), attnpos tables over several window fills (each fill's length patched to the window padded to whole elements times its own words a row, its offset to its compiled in-row base plus the window's first row), and kvslice - 1 rows of KV slack. stream_patch.hpp's kvslice parts are phlegm's own header's (open_kernels/harness), without its rb_win, slot and attnposv additions. kvslice_patch_test checks Gemma 4's local (four fills, 1024-row window) and global (two fills) streams at positions 0..4095. Gemma 4's dx_local / dx kernels carry kvslice 4 (recipes/gemma4.py dx_attention); the test covers 2 and 4. A diff over base plus the eight earlier Gemma 4 patches

gptoss_runtime_20261031.note: GPT-OSS from the GGUF (OPEN-FAMILY-GPTOSS, recipes/gptoss.py): the MXFP4 GGUF type (39); a GGUF embedding row and an F32 norm zero-extended into a padded width; pack ops gx_q8 (Q8_0 -> q8 half-tiles, the bias in the pad), gx_ug / gx_down (MXFP4 experts -> half-tiles, up | gate per band), gx_lmhead (Q8_0 -> lm_head_q8's f32-scale chunks), the same bytes as recipes/gptoss_pack.py; the gptoss_route program step (the router on the host between gx_att and gx_moe: top-k, softmax over the chosen, weights and weighted down biases into act, moe2_apply on gx_moe's fills) and host_step dispatching it beside moeroute2; arm_route_records limited to moeroute2 steps. A diff over base plus the nine Gemma 4 patches

gemma4_moe_20261031.note: Gemma 4 26B-A4B from its QAT Q4_0 GGUF (OPEN-FAMILY-GEMMA4-MOE, recipes/gemma4.py): pack ops g4_q40 (Q4_0 2-D / expert 3-D tensors into Q4_0-native band-law chunks, zero-padded rows and columns, expert and band strides) and g4_lmhead_q8 (the Q6_K tied embedding requantised to lm_head_q8's bf16-scale chunks); program steps gemma4_route (host router, top 8 renormalised * per_expert_scale, pre_ffw_norm_2 into gm_moe's input, moeroute2 patch) and gemma4_combine (post_ffw_norm of t1 + post_ffw_norm_2(m), folded layer scalar, into xres); host_step; arm_route_records limited to moeroute2 steps; gguf_pack_test cases. A diff over base plus the nine Gemma 4 patches (independent of gptoss-runtime.patch); built in target/npu-dev/gemma4-moe-runtime

gemma4_moe_decode_20261101.note: Gemma 4 26B-A4B decode (OPEN-FAMILY-GEMMA4-MOE, 2026-11-01): gemma4_route's router over the host threads with eight partial sums a logit (7-9 ms -> ~1 ms a token, logits byte-identical); gemma4_combine's moe_parts (m = the sum of that many partials, for the gm8 probe); OFLM_G4_SPLIT host-split timers. sha256 e1cd6b793d05c8fd1534bdc131e05b92f03aa95f2036aafce34bf452cc0abab9; built in target/npu-dev/gemma4-moe-runtime

qwen35moe_gguf_20261031.note: Qwen3.5 / 3.6 MoE straight from a llama.cpp qwen35moe GGUF (OPEN-FAMILY-QWEN36MOE-GGUF, recipes/qwen36moe.py gguf_view): pack ops q35_mat / q35_stripes / q35_down / q35_lmhead / q35_t / q35_vec / q35_conv write the q4nx ops' bytes in the q4_1 law (Q4_0 / Q4_1 / Q4_K codes kept, scale pair bf16 RNE; Q8_0 / Q5_0 / Q6_K requantized), with the per-head [q | gate] split and the linear-attention value-head untile (PackOp period / take / offset / kheads / vperk / vdim / v0 / vaxis); the Q5_0 size in gguf_type_bytes; op_region accepts q35_mat; the MoE block route's host stages read their small weights from the packed consts on a GGUF; q35_pack_dump (no XRT) for open_kernels/model/qwen35moe_gguf_check.py. A diff over base plus the nine Gemma 4 patches and gptoss-runtime.patch (sha256 8a5f808e..., as recorded, not the gptoss-runtime working tree)

gptoss_prefill_runtime_20261031.note: GPT-OSS's native MXFP4 experts and block prefill (OPEN-FAMILY-GPTOSS, OPEN-PREFILL-GPTOSS): pack ops gx_ug_mx4 / gx_down_mx4 (MXFP4 experts as mx4 half-tiles, the GGUF's nibbles re-signed for gemv_mx4.h), gp_bfp16 (a GGUF tensor's rows into a gemm_bfp16 B operand at any 64-multiple K, split hi / lo) and gp_mx4 (MXFP4 experts as gemm_bfp16 GB_B=mx4 tiles); the manifest's gptoss_prefill section and the gxexpert stream patch (an expert GEMM's buffer-0 fills re-pointed per dispatch, two stream copies alternating); Core::step_gptoss_prompt, the layer-major route behind step_gemm_prompt / layer_major_ok; block_prefill_min and the engine's use of it.
